t: If a unit vector is represented by 0.5î+0.8ĵ+ck̂, then the value of c is
s:
Concept:
A unit vector has a magnitude equal to 1. For any vector A = xî + yĵ + zk̂, its magnitude is calculated as |A| = √(x² + y² + z²).

Calculation:
|û| = √(0.5² + 0.8² + c²) = 1
Squaring both sides:
0.25 + 0.64 + c² = 1
0.89 + c² = 1
c² = 1 - 0.89 = 0.11
c = √0.11

Options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect because substituting them gives a magnitude different from 1 (for example, c = 1 gives a magnitude of √1.89 ≠ 1).

Correct Answer: (C) √0.11

t: The resultant of P⃗ and Q⃗ is R⃗. If Q⃗ is doubled, R⃗ is doubled; when Q⃗ is reversed, R⃗ is again doubled. Find P :Q:R
s:
Let θ be the angle between P⃗ and Q⃗. Then
R²=|P⃗+Q⃗|²=P²+Q²+2PQcosθ …(i)
Then If Q⃗ is doubled, R⃗ is doubled.
That means, the magnitude of resultant of 2Q⃗ and P⃗ is
(2R)²=P²+(2Q)²+2P(PQ)cosθ
This yields 4R²=P²+4Q²+4PQcosθ …(ii)
When Q⃗ is reversed, R⃗ is doubled.
Hence, the magnitude of resultant of P⃗ and (−Q⃗) is 2R
Then (2R)²=P²+Q²+2PQcos(180°−θ)
This yields 4R²=P²+Q²−2PQcosθ …(iii)
yields 3Q²+2PQcosθ=3R² …(iv)
+ (iii) yields P²+Q²=5R²/2 …(v)
+ (iv) yields P²+4Q²=7R² …(vi)
Solving (v) and (vi), we obtain Q=√(3/2)R and P=R.
Hence, P:Q:R=√2:√3:√2

t: In an experiment for determining density (ρ) of a rectangular metal block, a student makes the following measurements. Find the value of ρ (in gcm⁻³) up to appropriate significant figures, stating the uncertainty in the value of ρ.
s:
ρ=m/xyz=39.3/(5.12×2.56×0.37)=8.1037 g cm⁻³
(Δρ/δ)ₘₐₓ=Δm/m+Δx/x+Δy/y+Δz/z
=0.1/39.3+0.01/5.12+0.01/2.56+0.01/0.37
=0.0353
∴ Δρ=0.0353×ρ=0.0353×8.1037
=0.286gcm⁻³
Round off error Δρ to the first significant figure as Δρ=0.3gcm⁻³
Hence ρ=8.1037gm⁻³ is not accurate to the fourth decimal place. In fact, it is accurate only up to the first decimal place. Hence the value of ρ much be rounded off as 8.1 and the result of the measurement is written as
ρ=(8.1±0.3)gcm⁻³

t: The coefficient of viscosity (η) of a liquid by the method of flow through a capillary tube is given by the formula η=π/8R⁴/lP/Q where R= radius of the capillary tube, l= length of the tube, P= pressure difference between its ends, and Q= volume of liquid flowing per second. Which quantity must be measured most accurately?
s:
The correct choice is (a).
The maximum permissible error in η is given by the relation
Δη/η=4ΔR/R+Δl/l+ΔP/P+ΔQ/Q
It is clear that the error in the measurement of R is magnified four times on account of the occurrence of R⁴ in the formula. Hence the radius (R) of the capillary tube must be measured most accurately. Thus the quantity which is raised to the highest power needs the most accurate measurement. !

s:
vec(OC) and vec(OA) are equal in magnitude and inclined to each other at an angle of 90°. So, their resultant is √2r. It acts mid-way between vec(OC) and vec(OA), i.e., along OB
Now, both r and √2r are along the same line and in the same direction.

t: Given that A⃗+B⃗=C⃗⋅ If |A⃗|=4,|B⃗|=5 and |C⃗|=√61 The angle between A⃗ and B⃗ is
s:

vec((A)+B⃗)⋅(A⃗+B⃗)=C⃗⋅C⃗
⇒ A²+B²+2ABcosθ=C²
⇒ 4²+5²=2×4×5cosθ=61
⇒cosθ=1/2⇒θ=60° .
